conventions.leaf: {prim, params, transform: {rotate: [{axis: x|y|z|[x,y,z], deg}], translate: [x,y,z]}}; rotations apply in list order, then the translation
conventions.node: {op: union|subtract|intersect, children: [a, b]}; subtract is children[0] minus children[1]
conventions.cylinder: params {radius, height}; axis +Z from z=0 to z=height
conventions.cone: params {r1 (at z=0), r2 (at z=height), height}; r1 or r2 may be 0 (apex)
conventions.torus: params {major, minor}; axis +Z, centred on the origin
conventions.prism: params {points: [[x,y],...] simple polygon, height}; extruded +Z from z=0
conventions.brep: params {source: gzipped wonky-acceptance-operands/1 JSON, body: index}; the exact B-rep body as stored (identity transform); tessellated by scripts/bakeoff/brep-tessellate.mjs
conventions.deviationMm: stated bound on the distance between a leaf tessellation and its analytic surface
conventions.expect: solid (a valid closed 2-manifold mesh, possibly several components) | empty (valid answer is an ok mesh with 0 triangles) | non-manifold-contact (the exact result touches itself along a line or point; a closed 2-manifold mesh of it does not exist, so the expected answer is unresolved with a reason; a mesh is reported but not scored as a pass)

cases.fdmRationale: Horizontal bore whose wall breaks the top face by 0.005 mm (< deviation); the inscribed polygon does not break it, so the mesh topology (closed bore, genus 1) differs from the exact CSG (open slot, genus 0).
Round boss 0.005 mm wider than the bar it sits on; exact result has two thin cylinder slivers, the inscribed polygon stays inside the bar.
Flush lip whose top is 1e-9 mm above the base top (below the 1e-7 carrier-merge tolerance).
Flush lip whose top is 1e-6 mm above the base top (above the merge tolerance): a 1e-6 mm step face.
Lip top 1.5e-7 mm above the base top: just above the 1e-7 mm carrier-merge tolerance.
Plate with a through hole, whole part in a random orientation (x 23.7, y 41.3, z 11.1 deg).
Two blocks, each in its own random orientation, overlapping in general position.
plate-through-hole scaled by 1e-3 (40 x 30 x 5 um plate) with deviation 1e-5 mm: absolute tolerances become relatively coarse.
plate-through-hole scaled by 1e3 (40 m plate) at deviation 0.01 mm: 1260-gon hole, coordinates 4e4 mm.
The same hole drilled three times plus a self-union of the plate (coincident carriers from four leaves).
Intersection of two disjoint blocks: the answer is the empty solid.
A cylinder minus a larger block that contains it: empty.
Three separate parts on one plate (block, rotated pin, frustum): three components.
Slot / stadium plate: a block with two half-round ends; plane/cylinder G1 edges along the tangent lines.
Two holes whose walls touch along a line (pitch = diameter); the plate pinches to zero width there.
A 0.005 mm chamfer chip on one cube corner (one triangle, every vertex within deviation of all three neighbouring planes: the sliver rule applies to a real face).
Coaxial cylinders of radius 5 and 5 - 1e-6: a 1e-6 mm tube wall (near-coincident, not merged).
Hole whose wall comes within 1e-6 mm of the side face (a quarter-turn polygon vertex sits 1e-6 mm inside the face).
Hole wall 1e-9 mm from the side face.
Six bars rotated in 15 deg steps about one centre (iterated union, many near-degenerate triangles near the centre).
Two blocks whose top faces cross at 0.1 deg (nearly coplanar, transverse edge).
plate-countersink rotated 90 deg about x then 30 deg about z: sliver rule under rotation.
Block with a fully enclosed spherical cavity (a sphere face with no edges at all, as an inner void shell).
A whole ball next to a block: an outer shell made of one boundary-less sphere face.
Ball with a 0.005 mm deep flat (cap height < deviation): the flat disk is 0.316 mm across.
Ball with two perpendicular flats meeting in an edge: the sphere face is one loop of two arcs with two vertices.
Ball intersected with a randomly rotated block whose corner lies inside the ball: three flats meeting in a corner, sphere loop of three oblique arcs.
Ball with an off-centre through hole: sphere/cylinder non-coaxial (space quartic). Correct answer is a named refusal.
Ball with a centred bore whose axis is 1e-6 mm off the centre (above the 1e-7 coaxial tolerance): exact curve is a quartic, not a circle.
Same with a 1e-9 mm offset (below the coaxial tolerance).
Randomly rotated torus cut in half by a plane through its axis: two meridian circles bound the torus face.
torus-minus-box with the whole part randomly rotated (latitude circles and meridian seam off the world axes).
Torus with its top shaved 2e-6 mm (plane near-tangent to the top circle): exact result has a 0.007 mm wide planar annulus.
Block with two separate sealed cavities: one solid, two void shells.
Hollow block with a loose cube floating inside the cavity (captive part): two solids, one with a void that contains the other.
Cavity whose top wall is 1e-6 mm thick (near-coincident planes 1e-6 apart, below the F32 spacing at 20 mm).
sphere-minus-box scaled by 1e-3 (10 um ball) with deviation 1e-5 mm.
sphere-minus-box scaled by 1e3 (10 m ball) at deviation 1 mm.
The same ball unioned three times, then flattened: coincident sphere carriers from three leaves.
Dome on a plate: the sphere centre lies exactly on the top face (great-circle rim) and the ball pokes out below the plate (two sphere faces on one carrier).
Two balls touching at one point (the poles coincide): the exact union is non-manifold; expected answer is a refusal.

Ice-cream cone (cone + ball on its axis), randomly rotated: the coaxial carriers meet in two candidate circles (z 3.2 r 3.6, the real edge, and the equator z 8 r 6, where the cone rim lies on the sphere), off the world axes.

Cylinder minus a box whose face is 1e-5 rad off parallel to the axis and shaves 0.005 mm off the side (< deviation). tangent.bend only checks plane/cylinder when |n.a| < 1e-12, so the tiny tilt skips the near-tangency test; the inscribed facet (sagitta 0.009) is never reached.
Control for the tilt bypass: the same 0.005 mm shave with the face exactly parallel to the axis; the near-tangency pre-check must refuse it.
Intersect variant of the tilt bypass: the exact result is the thin 0.005 mm shaving (a real solid); the mesh intersection is empty.
Rod minus a parallel rod (1e-5 rad off parallel) that grazes it by 0.005 mm: cylinder/cylinder is only checked for |1-cos| < 1e-12.
Rod minus a perpendicular rod that grazes it 0.006 mm deep (< the 0.0096 mm sagitta): crossed cylinders are never near-tangency candidates; the exact result has a small quartic dent.
Torus (R10 r2, 50 minor segments so no vertex ring on top) minus a box shaving 0.003 mm off the top: torus/plane is not checked; the exact result has a flat annulus 0.22 mm wide.
Torus intersect the same box: the exact result is a thin annular cap (non-empty solid); the mesh intersection is empty.
Frustum (r 5 -> 2 over 20) minus a box whose face is parallel to a generator and shaves 0.003 mm (plane/cone parabola region): cones are not near-tangency checked.
The cone shave under a random rotation (37.3 deg about (0.3,-0.7,0.64), then 11.9 deg about z).
Plate 2x2x1 with a pin of diameter 0.2 mm standing 0.005 mm proud (8-segment band of 16 triangles).
Plate 2x2x1 with a 0.2 mm diameter pocket 0.005 mm deep.
The micro pin under the random rotation.
Box plus a separate disc 0.2 mm in diameter and 0.005 mm thick (two bodies).
Two blocks 0.005 mm apart joined by a 0.005 mm cube bridge at a corner: one body, genus 0.
Two overlapping boxes whose tops differ by 3e-6 mm (just above the 1e-6 plane window): a 3 um step face made of needle triangles.
Box with an internal box void whose top wall is 3e-6 mm thick (planar; valid thin wall).
Plate minus a hole tilted 23 deg, all under the random rotation (general-position ellipses).
Plate 20 m x 20 m x 4 m minus a 3 m hole (deviation 1 mm).
Two boxes sharing only a face, intersected: the regularized result is empty.
Plate minus the same rotated hole three times ((P - H) - H) - H, all under the random rotation.
The exactly parallel control under the random rotation: the pre-check must still see the pair as parallel (F32x2 rotated normals) and refuse.
Union variant of the tilt bypass: the mesh has two bodies 0.004 mm apart; the clearance certificate should refuse.
Control: the torus shave with the default 48 minor segments (a vertex ring on top), so the mesh does cut the annulus.
Control: the cone shave with a vertex line on the shaved generator, so the mesh cuts a sliver (plane/cone parabola region).

2 mm cube with a 0.09 mm corner chip (one triangular face, all points within 0.09 of its 3 neighbour planes). FDM-typical deviation 0.1. The mesh is exact (planes only), so dropping the chip is a recovery error, not a mesh error.
1 mm cube (small pin head) with a 0.0095 mm corner chip at the corpus deviation 0.01.
Union of a 2 mm cube and a 0.5 mm cube turned corner-up whose apex pokes 0.05 mm through the top: a 3-faced planar tip (edges 0.087 mm) that the exact mesh has; deviation 0.1.
The planar corner bump under a random rotation.
Plate 6x6x1 minus a flat cone (r 2.5, h 0.25, 16 segments at deviation 0.05) whose apex enters the bottom 0.045 mm: a conical dimple of radius 0.45 mm, exactly meshed (16 fan triangles, apex exact).
Plate 6x6x1 union the same flat cone whose apex pokes 0.045 mm above the top, under a random rotation.
Cone standing on its apex exactly on the plate top: the exact union touches in one point (non-manifold); the answer must be a refusal.

Cylinder r5 minus a box face shaving 0.005 mm off its side, tilted 1e-8 rad (the face moves < 2e-7 mm over the 20 mm rod). tangent.bend requires |n.a| < 1e-12, so this is not a candidate while the parallel control is.
plate-through-hole translated by (1e5, -1e5, 5e4) mm (a part placed far from the origin).
cylinder-tangent-box-face translated by (1e5, -1e5, 5e4): the clearance certificate must still refuse the line contact.
Box 10^3 minus a sphere r3 (void) union a ball r2.9 (island) concentric: three shells, two solids, gap 0.1 mm.
Funnel (45 deg cone cut from a box) with a ball r2 sitting 0.004 mm clear of the cone: two bodies. Sphere/cone pairs are not near-tangency checked.
Cylinder minus itself turned by 360 deg about a tilted axis (1e-16-level perturbation): exact result is empty.
Plate minus a hole minus the same hole shifted 1e-12 mm (below the coincidence epsilon).
Intersection of a disjoint cone and sphere under a random rotation: empty.
plate-countersink scaled by 1e-3 (30 um plate) at deviation 1e-5: absolute 1e-6/1e-7/1e-9 tolerances meet micro scale.

Regression (fix#2 of the hybrid gate): rod minus a plane tilted 5e-4 along the axis (0.015 mm deep at z=0, crossing the facets; 0.005 mm at z=20, inside the facets), then minus the half z<12 that holds every crossing. The exact result keeps a 0.45-0.6 mm flat strip on z in [12,20]; the meshes have none, and the leaf tessellations of the (plane, cylinder) pair still cross in the removed half. recover must refuse, not write a plain cylinder segment (volume 628.3185 against the exact 628.2986).

Control for adv-graze-crossing-removed: rod minus a 30 deg tilted cut crossing z in [2,8], then minus z<12. Every crossing is removed and the remaining rod is far from the cut plane: exact (a plain cylinder segment), no refusal.
